results: 1. Complete physical examination, including vital signs.
cranial nerve examination: right oculomotor nerve palsy with exotropia, hypotropia, impaired right eye movements, mild anisocoria, and right ptosis
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
lid position and measurement (MRD1 both sides): not recorded
sustained upgaze fatigability test: no fatigable droop
ocular motility examination: exotropia, hypotropia and motility impairment - a right oculomotor nerve palsy

pupil examination (size, light reaction): mild anisocoria; the RIGHT pupil is unreactive to dim light, with involuntary pupillary spasms that are irregular in both frequency and duration and unrelated to eye position
visual acuity and colour vision: normal
pain and periorbital inspection: no pain, no swelling, no discolouration
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Right pupil-involving oculomotor nerve palsy, most concerning for compression by a posterior communicating artery aneurysm

Cyclic/aberrantly regenerating right oculomotor nerve palsy, possibly related to prior neurosurgery
